Unique surrogate identifier for each curative action record within the title production operations domain. Primary key for this entity.
Reference to the party (curative specialist, title examiner, or external vendor) responsible for executing this curative action. Supports workload and aging analysis.

Foreign key linking to property.easement_restriction. Business justification: Curative actions address easement and restriction issues (missing releases, ambiguous language, encroachments, HOA violations).

Foreign key linking to property.encumbrance. Business justification: Curative actions resolve specific encumbrances (mortgages, judgments, tax liens). Processors track payoff demands, release instruments, and satisfaction recordings per encumbrance.

Foreign key linking to recording.recording_submission. Business justification: Curative actions often result in resubmissions after recording rejection (corrected docs, additional signatures). Tracks curative-to-resubmission cycle time per VREQ-016.

Reference to the title examination finding (defect, lien, encumbrance, or cloud on title) that triggered this curative action, if applicable.
Reference to the parent title order under which this curative action is being performed. Links the curative step to the originating transaction.
Reference to the Schedule B-I title requirement or defect that this curative action is intended to clear. Owned by the underwriting domain.

Current lifecycle state of the curative action. Drives clearance cycle-time metrics and closing readiness dashboards. Transitions: open → in_progress → pending_receipt → completed or waived.
Classification of the curative step required to clear the defect or requirement. Examples include obtain release, record reconveyance, obtain payoff, record satisfaction, obtain affidavit.
Method by which the title defect or requirement was ultimately cleared. Supports curative action effectiveness analysis and underwriting exception rate metrics per VREQ-016.
Calendar date on which the curative action was marked complete and the associated requirement or defect was cleared. Null if not yet completed.
Indicates whether this curative action is specifically addressing a chain-of-title break (gap in the grantor-grantee index or missing conveyance). Supports COT break metrics per VREQ-016.
Timestamp when this curative action record was first created in the title production system. Audit field supporting record provenance and lifecycle tracking.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for monetary amounts on this curative action record. Typically USD for domestic US title transactions.
Number of calendar days this curative action has been open as of the last update. Stored for aging bucket reporting; supports open and aging title requirements metrics per VREQ-016.
Underwriter-assigned severity rating of the title defect being cured. Critical defects block commitment issuance; high defects require UW referral; medium and low may be handled operationally.
Classification of the underlying title defect or encumbrance being cured (e.g., tax lien, mechanics lien, judgment lien, lis pendens, HOA lien, unreleased mortgage, chain-of-title break).
Target date by which this curative action must be completed to support the scheduled closing date. Drives SLA monitoring and closing readiness metrics.
Indicates whether the curative instrument was submitted via electronic recording (eRecording) gateway (e.g., Simplifile, CSC eRecording) rather than physical submission.
Date on which this curative action was escalated to underwriting, management, or legal due to inability to clear within standard processing. Null if not escalated.
Indicates whether the documentary evidence required to confirm clearance of the defect or requirement has been received and imaged into the document management system.
Date on which the curative evidence document was received and confirmed by the title operations team. Supports evidence completeness and provenance metrics per VREQ-016.

description: Number of calendar days of lapsed E&O coverage between the prior policy expiration and the current policy effective date. Zero or null when no gap exists. Used for risk scoring.

business_glossary_term: Errors and Omissions (E&O) Days Until Expiration

description: Date on which the E&O policy coverage expires. Triggers renewal workflow and agent authority suspension if not renewed prior to expiration.

business_glossary_term: Errors and Omissions (E&O) Minimum Required Aggregate Limit

Unique surrogate identifier for each curative action record within the claims administration system. Primary key for the claim_curative_action entity.

FK to underwriting.curative_action.curative_action_id — Links claim-phase curative to the underwriting curative SSOT with a claim-context discriminator so claim curative aging ties to the single curative source.

Foreign key linking to property.easement_restriction. Business justification: Curative actions for easement disputes, encroachments, or CC&R violations reference specific easement/restriction records.
Foreign key linking to property.encumbrance. Business justification: Many curative actions resolve specific encumbrances (mortgage payoffs, lien releases, judgment satisfactions).

Foreign key linking to property.parcel. Business justification: Curative actions (lien releases, corrective deeds, boundary agreements) must reference the specific parcel for recording submission, legal description matching, and APN validation.
Reference to the internal staff member (claim handler, title examiner, or curative specialist) responsible for executing and tracking this curative action.
Self-referencing identifier pointing to the immediately preceding version of this curative action record, supporting lifecycle revision history and audit trail per VREQ-007.
Reference to the eRecording gateway submission record (Simplifile/CSC) tracking the submission, acceptance, or rejection of the curative instrument at the county recorder.
Reference to the parent title insurance claim under which this curative action was initiated. Links the action to the FNOL and investigation record.
Reference to the specific title defect, encumbrance, or cloud on title identified during examination or claim investigation that this curative action is intended to resolve.
Reference to the issued owner or lender title policy (OTP/LTP) under which coverage is being asserted and curative action is being pursued.
Reference to the Schedule B-I requirement, if any, that corresponds to this curative action. Null when the action arises solely from a post-policy claim investigation.

Foreign key linking to underwriting.underwriting_title_examination. Business justification: Claim curative teams review the original examination to understand the defect's history, prior curative attempts, and whether the defect was identified but not
Reference to the underwriting referral or policy exception record created when this curative action requires underwriter approval. Null when uw_referral_required is false.
reference: Underwriting Risk and Policy Management System

description: Free-text narrative describing the specific curative steps being taken, the parties involved, and the legal instruments or proceedings required to clear the identified defect.
Externally visible, human-readable identifier for this curative action, used in correspondence with courts, county recorders, and opposing counsel. Format: CA-YYYY-NNNNNN.

Current lifecycle state of the curative action: open (initiated), in_progress (work underway), pending_recording (instrument prepared, awaiting county acceptance), resolved (defect cleared), withdrawn, or escalated.
reference: ALTA Best Practices; NAIC Claims Reporting

description: Classification of the curative remedy being pursued. Examples: lien release, deed correction, quiet title suit, probate proceeding, affidavit of heirship, reconveyance.
Total actual expenditure incurred to complete this curative action. Compared against estimated cost for reserve accuracy and loss ratio reporting.
Calendar date on which the curative action was confirmed resolved and the underlying defect or requirement was cleared. Null if still open.
reference: ALTA Best Practices; NAIC Claims Reporting

business_glossary_term: Chain of Title Break Flag (COT Break)
description: Indicates whether the underlying defect involves a break in the chain of title (COT), such as a missing grantor-grantee link, unrecorded conveyance, or vesting discrepancy.
ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the estimated and actual cost amounts. Typically USD for domestic US title insurance transactions.
Name of the court or judicial jurisdiction (county, state, federal district) in which litigation for this curative action has been filed.
System timestamp when this curative action record was first created in the claims administration system. Supports audit trail and provenance requirements.
Type of legal instrument produced or obtained to effect the cure (e.g., release of lien, corrective deed, satisfaction of judgment, reconveyance deed, court order).
reference: ALTA; County Recorder / Register of Deeds

description: Number of calendar days this curative action has been in an open or in-progress state, calculated from initiated_date. Supports curative action aging and effectiveness metrics per VREQ-016.
Classification of the underlying title defect or encumbrance being cured (e.g., mechanics lien, judgment lien, tax lien, HOA lien, chain-of-title break, missing heir, forged deed, encroachment).
reference: ALTA; NAIC Title Insurance Loss Cause Codes

description: Date on which this curative action was escalated to senior underwriting counsel, litigation, or management due to complexity, aging, or reserve impact. Null if not escalated.
Estimated total cost to complete this curative action, including legal fees, court costs, recording fees, and vendor charges. Used for reserve adequacy and loss exposure analysis.
Reference identifier or URI to the document management system record containing supporting evidence for this curative action (e.g., signed release, court order, recorded instrument image).
Indicates whether this curative action specifically addresses a gap period risk — the interval between the last search date and the recording of the insured instrument.
Calendar date on which this curative action was formally initiated by the claim handler or title examiner. Used to measure curative aging and cycle time.
Official document number, book/page reference, or instrument number assigned by the county recorder upon acceptance of the curative instrument.
Date the curative instrument was officially recorded by the county recorder or register of deeds, establishing constructive notice and clearing the defect of record.
reference: County Recorder / Register of Deeds; ALTA

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this record represents the current active version of the curative action. False for superseded historical revisions. Supports lifecycle history per VREQ-007.
System timestamp of the most recent modification to this curative action record. Used for change detection in ETL pipelines and audit compliance.
Face amount of the lien, judgment, or encumbrance being cured. Used to assess claim severity and negotiate payoff or release amounts with lienholders.
reference: NAIC Title Insurance Loss Cause Reporting

description: Court-assigned case number for quiet title actions, probate proceedings, or other litigation initiated as part of this curative action. Null for non-litigated cures.
Indicates whether outside legal counsel has been retained to pursue this curative action (e.g., quiet title litigation, probate proceedings, or contested lien releases).
Name of the external law firm or attorney retained to handle this curative action. Populated only when outside_counsel_engaged is true.
Negotiated or agreed payoff amount required to obtain a release or satisfaction of the lien or encumbrance. May differ from the original lien amount due to negotiation or accrued interest.
Business priority assigned to this curative action, reflecting urgency relative to closing readiness, policy issuance lag, or claim reserve exposure.
Indicates whether the curative instrument must be recorded with the county recorder or register of deeds to be effective against third parties and to clear the title defect.

description: Amount actually recovered through subrogation, indemnification, or third-party contribution related to this curative action. Reduces net loss on the parent claim.
